BUGS: (a) the bodyTitle (+T) affordance is rendered (FootnoteCard.tsx:123-124 onBodyTitleChange=onEditTitle) and editable, but onEditTitle -> handleEditFootnoteTitle is a NO-OP in the main app (EditorPane.tsx:2740-2744, the ONLY definition, wired into every main render path 3437/3510/3632/4397/4617 and omni omni.tsx:18,47) AND the serializer never emits `title` (latex-serializer.ts:393) — so a typed footnote title is silently discarded with no persistence path anywhere. findings.subject: footnotes
findings.symptom: The footnote card's title (+T) affordance lets the user type a title, but the title is silently discarded — it is never stored on the footnote, never persisted, and never reappears (the collapsed-card title row stays blank and the +T affordance returns on the next render).
findings.suspectedRootCause: End-to-end dead path. The panel/omni surface a CardBodyTitle +T input on every footnote (FootnoteCard.tsx:123-124 passes onBodyTitleChange={onEditTitle ?? undefined}; in the main app onEditTitle is truthy so the input renders). On blur it calls onChange(v) -> the panel's onEditTitle(id,title) -> FootnotesHost.onEditTitle (footnotes-host.tsx:51) -> EditorPane.handleEditFootnoteTitle, which is the ONLY definition of that handler and is an explicit no-op (EditorPane.tsx:2740-2744 'Wired as a no-op until the main app needs it'). The EditorHandle DOES expose updateFootnoteTitle (Editor.tsx:1079-1099) that would setNodeMarkup the node's `title` attr, but NOTHING in the codebase calls it (grep: zero callers). Even if it were wired, the footnote LaTeX serializer emits only `\footnote{content}` and drops the `title` attr entirely (latex-serializer.ts:389-394), so the title would not round-trip to .tex and would be lost on the next parse cycle (the parser reconstructs the node with the default empty title). So the affordance is functional-looking but inert: getFootnotes() always reads node.attrs.title==='' (Editor.tsx:1039) and CardBodyTitle is uncontrolled (defaultValue, panel-primitives.tsx:552) so the typed text persists only visually until the next re-render.

evidence.note: handleEditFootnoteTitle = useCallback((_id,_title) => {}) — the ONLY footnote-title handler; a no-op, wired into all main render paths (3437/3510/3632/4397/4617)
bodyTitle={fn.title} + onBodyTitleChange={onEditTitle ?? undefined} — the +T input IS rendered and editable
updateFootnoteTitle exists on the EditorHandle (would setNodeMarkup title) but has ZERO callers anywhere in src/
footnote case serializes only `\footnote{richJsonToLatex(content)}` with the vfid marker — the `title` attr is never emitted, so it cannot round-trip to .tex even if set
CardBodyTitle input is uncontrolled (defaultValue) — the typed title shows until re-render, masking that it was dropped

reproSteps: Open a paper with a footnote; show the Footnotes panel; expand the footnote card.
Click the +T affordance and type a title (e.g. 'Methodology note'); press Enter or click away.
The title appears briefly in the input.
Collapse and re-expand the card (or switch panels and back) — the title is gone and the +T placeholder is back.
Reload the paper — no title; the .tex never recorded one.
findings.suspectedClass: Affordances rendered for a kind whose write-handler is an unwired stub. Check the same handleEdit*Title no-op pattern for any other panel that surfaces CardBodyTitle but routes to a stubbed handler; and check any node-attr (here `title`) that the panel can mutate but the LaTeX serializer does not round-trip (silent-drop-on-reparse class).

findings.subject: footnotes
findings.symptom: Edits to an orphaned footnote's body or title are kept only in volatile React state and are lost on reload; the orphan card itself also vanishes on reload (orphans are never persisted).
findings.suspectedRootCause: Orphaned footnotes live entirely in the `orphanedFootnotes` useState array (EditorLayout.tsx:1106), populated at runtime by the `virgil-footnote-orphaned` window event the orphan-detector fires when a non-empty footnote node is deleted (footnote.ts:200-214). The orphan edit handlers (useOrphanActions) only setOrphanedFootnotes — handleEditOrphan maps content, handleEditOrphanTitle maps title (orphans.ts:24-40) — with NO writeSidecar / persistence call. There is no orphan sidecar: the footnotes.json sidecar (useFootnotes) tracks anchored/sidecar entries and 'unanchored' refs that survive syncFromEditor (useFootnotes.ts:127), but the panel does NOT render from that hook for orphans — it renders the event-sourced orphanedFootnotes state. So on a full reload the doc no longer contains the deleted atom, the orphan event never re-fires, and the orphan (with any edits) is gone. This is partly by-design (orphans are a transient 'you deleted the marker, here is the rescued body' affordance), but the panel exposes a full editable RichTextField + title on the orphan card (OrphanedFootnoteCard, FootnoteCard.tsx:210-245), inviting edits that are then silently discarded.

evidence.note: handleEditOrphan / handleEditOrphanTitle only setOrphanedFootnotes(state); no sidecar write
orphan creation is purely state from the virgil-footnote-orphaned event; nothing persists it
orphanedFootnotes = useState([]) — volatile, reset on every mount (key={docId} remounts on doc switch)
OrphanedFootnoteCard mounts a full editable RichTextField + onEditTitle — the user is invited to edit a non-persisted card

reproSteps: In a paper, delete a footnote's in-text marker (leaving non-empty body) so it appears as an orphan card in the Footnotes panel.
Expand the orphan and edit its body and/or add a title.
Reload the paper (or switch documents and back).
Observe: the orphan card is gone entirely, and any body/title edits made to it are lost.
findings.suspectedClass: Editable cards backed by volatile-only state (no sidecar). Any panel that surfaces an editor on an item it never persists has this loss class — check examples-panel derived items and any 'rescued from deletion' transient card.

findings.subject: footnotes
findings.symptom: On a freshly-loaded paper, every footnote card's number badge in the Footnotes panel shows '0' (and every in-text marker shows '1'), instead of the correct 1,2,3,... — the numbers only become correct after the user adds, removes, reorders, or edits a footnote.
findings.suspectedRootCause: Footnote numbering is computed lazily by the renumber appendTransaction plugin, which is gated on a structural footnote diff (footnote.ts:220-247: addedFootnotes||removedFootnotes||footnoteOrderChanged). On doc load the editor is constructed with `content: initialContent` (Editor.tsx:462) — not via a docChanged transaction — and the DocStructureObserver's init runs buildInitial which emits NO diff (observer-plugin.ts:130-134; apply only diffs on tr.docChanged). The LaTeX parser writes number:0 for every footnote (latex-parser.ts:404,425) and getFootnotes() surfaces node.attrs.number||0 (Editor.tsx:1037). The panel's BadgeLabel renders fn.number directly with no fallback (FootnoteCard.tsx:122, panel-primitives.tsx:288-293) → '0'. The in-text NodeView uses `number||'1'` (footnote.ts:266) → '1'. So before any footnote op, panel shows '0' and text shows '1' (and all footnotes share the same wrong value). The state self-heals once any structural footnote op (including a body edit, which surfaces as footnoteOrderChanged per step-inspector.ts:399) triggers the appendTransaction renumber. renumberFootnotes() is NOT called on load (only from card-creation.ts).

evidence.note: parser sets number:0 for every \footnote (and 425 for \thanks)
state.init returns buildInitial(doc) with pendingDiff:null; apply bails on !tr.docChanged — so no diff exists at load
renumber appendTransaction is gated on addedFootnotes||removedFootnotes||footnoteOrderChanged — none present on the initial mount
footnoteBadge=BadgeLabel label={fn.number} — renders 0 directly (no ||'1' fallback like the NodeView)
getFootnotes reads node.attrs.number||0 — surfaces 0 to the panel

reproSteps: Open a paper that already contains 2+ footnotes (do not add/edit any yet).
Open the Footnotes panel.
Observe each footnote card's left badge reads '0' (all the same), while the in-text markers read '1'.
Add or edit any footnote — the appendTransaction renumber now runs and the badges correct to 1,2,3,...
LIVE STEP TO CONFIRM: open virgil-data/doc_devtest, count footnotes, and read the panel badges before touching any footnote; confirm they show 0 vs the 1.. in the body.
findings.suspectedClass: Lazily-computed display attributes that are only refreshed by a structural diff and never seeded on load. Citation ordering / example numbering use the same observer-diff cadence — verify they show correct ordinals on a freshly-loaded paper before any edit (initial-population class flagged in AGENTS.md keystroke-sanctity).

findings.subject: footnotes
findings.symptom: In a paper that contains a \thanks{} acknowledgement, creating any new footnote re-numbers the document so that the acknowledgement consumes footnote number 1 and every real footnote is shifted up by one (the first real footnote shows '2' in the text), and the wrong numbering persists.
findings.suspectedRootCause: Two divergent renumber implementations disagree on \thanks handling. The canonical appendTransaction renumber sets thanks footnotes to number:0 and does NOT advance the counter for them (footnote.ts:235-244), so acknowledgements are excluded from footnote numbering — matching LaTeX. But the imperative EditorHandle.renumberFootnotes() walks ALL footnotes and assigns counter++ to every one regardless of `thanks` (Editor.tsx:1171-1176). This imperative version is invoked on EVERY footnote creation (card-creation.ts:528 adopt-path, 550 normal-path). Its dispatched setNodeMarkup changes only `number`, which footnoteChanged detects (step-inspector.ts:268) but feeds `changedFootnotes`, NOT `footnoteOrderChanged` — and the appendTransaction renumber is gated on order/add/remove, not changedFootnotes (footnote.ts:220-223) — so it does NOT re-fire to correct the mis-numbering. The wrong numbers therefore persist until a later genuine add/remove/reorder triggers the canonical pass.

evidence.note: renumberFootnotes: `let counter=1; for(...) setNodeMarkup(pos,{...attrs,number:counter++})` — increments for thanks footnotes too (no thanks skip)
canonical renumber: if f.thanks set number:0 and do NOT advance num; else number=num++ — the correct LaTeX behavior the imperative path contradicts
handle.renumberFootnotes() called on the adopt-path of every footnote create (also 550)
footnoteOrderChanged only set when removed/added footnotes>0; a number-only setNodeMarkup does not set it, so the canonical renumber won't auto-correct the imperative mis-numbering

reproSteps: Open a paper whose \author{} contains a \thanks{...} acknowledgement and that has at least one \footnote.
Create a new footnote (toolbar / slash / typed).
Observe the acknowledgement now behaves as footnote #1 and the previously-first footnote shows '2' in the text; the panel reflects the shifted numbers.
The mis-numbering remains until a footnote is deleted/reordered.
findings.suspectedClass: Two implementations of one derived-numbering rule that drift on an edge case (here \thanks). Any 'imperative one-shot' vs 'observer-driven' pair (citation ordering, example sub-labels) is a candidate for the same divergence — audit whether the imperative path mirrors the appendTransaction's special-cases exactly.

findings.subject: footnotes
findings.symptom: The Footnotes panel/strip header count excludes orphaned footnotes — a panel showing only orphan cards displays no count badge at all, and a mixed panel undercounts by the number of orphans.
findings.suspectedRootCause: FootnotePanel passes count={footnotes.length} (anchored only) to CardListPanel (FootnotePanel.tsx:132), but the rendered `items` are orphans + anchored (FootnotePanel.tsx:112-121). PanelHeader only shows the count when >0 (panel-primitives.tsx:2088), so a panel with 0 anchored + N orphans shows nothing despite N cards. The header count and the visible card list disagree.

evidence.note: count={footnotes.length} — anchored only, excludes orphanedFootnotes
items merges orphanedFootnotes (first) + footnotes — the rendered set the count should reflect
PanelHeader hides the count entirely when count is 0

reproSteps: In a paper, delete all in-text footnote markers but keep their bodies so they become orphan cards.
Open the Footnotes panel.
Observe the orphan cards render but the header count badge is absent (count=0).
findings.suspectedClass: Header/strip count derived from a subset of the rendered list. Any panel that renders orphans + anchored but counts only anchored (or pending-AI-requests not counted) has the same count-vs-render mismatch.

findings.subject: footnotes
findings.symptom: Clicking a citation embedded inside a footnote body selects the correct citation card, but the card's vertical alignment can snap to a DIFFERENT citation instance (one in the main text or another footnote) when the same citation key appears more than once.
findings.suspectedRootCause: The footnote-body Citation NodeView dispatches virgil-citation-click with the citationId (citation.ts:269-287). The handler selects the card correctly (setSelectedCitationId, marker-clicks.ts:284) but resolves the alignment source element via document.querySelector('.citation-node[data-citation-id="X"]') (marker-clicks.ts:319-321), which returns the FIRST DOM node with that id. Citation nodes inside footnote-body mini-editors also set data-citation-id (citation.ts:256), and the same citationId can legitimately occur in several places. So the click's clickY is honored but the resolved sourceEl (used by alignOmniCardWithClick) may be a different occurrence, pulling the omni card to align with the wrong anchor. (The selection itself is correct; only the alignment target is ambiguous.)

evidence.note: footnote-body citation click dispatches virgil-citation-click with citationId + clickY + clickedPos (clickedPos is in the footnote mini-editor's coordinate space)
sourceEl = document.querySelector('.citation-node[data-citation-id=X]') — first match wins, ambiguous when the id repeats
the in-footnote citation NodeView also sets dom.dataset.citationId, so it is itself a querySelector candidate

reproSteps: Have a paper where one citation key is cited in the main body AND inside a footnote body (same citationId).
Click the citation rendered inside the footnote body.
The citation card is selected, but it vertically aligns to the first .citation-node occurrence (the main-text one) rather than the clicked in-footnote instance.
findings.suspectedClass: DOM lookups by a non-unique id attribute (document.querySelector first-match) when the same atom id is rendered on multiple surfaces. The same first-match alignment is used for footnote markers (marker-clicks.ts:263-265) and could mis-target if a footnote marker is mirrored across surfaces.

findings.subject: footnotes
findings.symptom: When a paper has multiple \thanks{} acknowledgements (e.g. one per author), every acknowledgement footnote card renders an identical 'A' badge and 'Acknowledgement' overline, with nothing to distinguish them in the panel.
findings.suspectedRootCause: Both the panel badge and the in-text marker hardcode 'A' for any thanks footnote (FootnoteCard.tsx:122 BadgeLabel label={fn.thanks ? 'A' : fn.number}; footnote.ts:266 dom.textContent = thanks ? 'A' : number) and the kind label override is the constant 'Acknowledgement' (FootnoteCard.tsx:116). The renumber pass deliberately sets thanks footnotes to number:0 (footnote.ts:235) so they carry no distinguishing ordinal, and there is no per-thanks sub-label. Multiple acknowledgements are therefore visually identical.

evidence.note: footnoteBadge = BadgeLabel label={fn.thanks ? 'A' : fn.number} — constant 'A' for all thanks
kindLabelOverride = fn.thanks ? 'Acknowledgement' : undefined — constant label
renumber sets thanks footnotes to number:0 (no ordinal), so there is no per-thanks distinguisher

reproSteps: Open a paper whose \author{} block has two or more \thanks{...} acknowledgements.
Open the Footnotes panel.
Observe both acknowledgement cards show the same 'A' badge and 'Acknowledgement' overline — only the body text differs.
findings.suspectedClass: Hardcoded badge glyph for a kind that can occur multiple times. Any kind whose marker text is a constant (rather than an ordinal) shows the same ambiguity when repeated.
